paper.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
truncated_sections: B.5 Performance Variance and Pass@k Rate

result.summary: 本文研究界面设计如何影响语言模型（LM）智能体在软件工程任务上的表现，并提出 SWE-agent 系统，为 LM 智能体提供专门设计的 agent-computer interface（ACI）[abstract][S1.p1]。SWE-agent 的 ACI 提供查看、搜索、编辑文件等简单动作，并配有护栏和简洁反馈，帮助智能体创建和编辑代码、浏览仓库、执行测试 [abstract][S1.p3]。在 SWE-bench 和 HumanEvalFix 上，SWE-agent 分别取得 12.5% 和 87.7% 的 pass@1 成绩，超过此前非交互式 LM 的最好结果 [abstract]。作者还通过消融实验分析了 ACI 设计选择对智能体行为和性能的影响 [S1.p4][S5.SS1.p1]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：LM 智能体在更复杂的软件工程任务上尚未被充分探索，而现有界面（如 Linux shell）是为人类用户设计的，LM 智能体作为一类新的终端用户可能有不同需求，因此需要研究界面设计如何影响 LM 智能体的表现 [S1.p1][S2.p1]。作者指出，LM 智能体直接与 Linux shell 交互时难以可靠地采取行动，例如无法提供编辑小段文件的简单命令，且无效编辑没有反馈，这些缺陷严重妨碍性能，从而促使设计 ACI [S1.p2]。

evidence.quote: However, applying agents to more complex code tasks like software engineering remains unexplored.
we investigate whether LM agents could similarly benefit from better-designed interfaces for performing software engineering tasks.
We argue that LM agents represent a new category of end user, with their own needs and abilities.
In practice, we find that LM agents can struggle to reliably take actions in this environment.
These deficits substantially hamper performance, motivating the need for an agent-computer interface (ACI)

method.text: 论文提出 SWE-agent，一个由 LM 和 ACI 组成的智能体，其 ACI 提供一小组简单动作用于查看、搜索和编辑文件，使用护栏防止常见错误，并在每一步给出具体简洁的反馈 [S1.p3]。ACI 包含搜索/导航、文件查看器、文件编辑器和上下文管理等组件，智能体每步生成一个 thought 和一个 command，再纳入命令执行反馈 [S3.p1]。设计方法上，作者假设 LM 固定，专注于设计 ACI，通过人工检查智能体行为发现问题并提出改进，以及网格搜索选择最佳 ACI 配置 [S2.p4]。

evidence.quote: SWE-agent’s ACI instead offers a small set of simple actions for viewing, searching through and editing files.
The ACI uses guardrails to prevent common mistakes, and an agent receives specific, concise feedback about a command’s effects at every turn.
The ACI comprises several principal components, including search/navigation, file viewer, file editor, and context management.
At each step, SWE-agent generates a thought and a command, then incorporates the feedback from the command’s execution in the environment
we assume a fixed LM and focus on designing the ACI to improve its performance
(1) manually inspect agent behavior to identify difficulties and propose improvements, and (2) run a grid search to select the best ACI configuration.

experiments.text: 实验主要在 SWE-bench 数据集上进行，该数据集包含来自 12 个流行 Python 包仓库的 2,294 个任务实例；消融和分析在 SWE-bench Lite 的 300 个实例上进行，另外还用 HumanEvalFix 测试基本代码编辑能力 [S4.p1]。所有结果、消融和分析基于 GPT-4 Turbo 和 Claude 3 Opus 两个 LM [S4.p2]。对比基线包括非交互式检索增强生成（RAG）基线和基于 Linux shell 的 Shell-only 基线 [S4.p3][S4.p4]。主要指标为 % Resolved 或 pass@1，并报告平均 API 推理成本，单实例预算设为 4 美元 [S4.p5]。

evidence.quote: We primarily evaluate on the SWE-bench dataset, which includes $2,294$ task instances from $12$ different repositories of popular Python packages.
SWE-bench Lite is a canonical subset of $300$ instances from SWE-bench
We also test SWE-agent’s basic code editing abilities with HumanEvalFix
All results, ablations, and analyses are based on two leading LMs, GPT-4 Turbo ( gpt-4-1106-preview) and Claude 3 Opus ( claude-3-opus-20240229).
The first setting is the non-interactive, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) baselines
The second setting, called Shell-only, is adapted from the interactive coding framework
We report % Resolved or pass $@$ $1$ as the main metric
we set the per-instance budget to $4; if a run exceeded this budget, existing edits were submitted automatically.

findings.text: SWE-agent 搭配 GPT-4 Turbo 在所有系统中表现最好，解决了完整 SWE-bench 测试集的 12.47%（286/2,294）和 Lite 子集的 18.00%（54/300）[S5.p1]。相比 Lite 上的 RAG，SWE-agent 成本高 8–13 倍，但 % Resolved 率提升 6.7 倍；相比 Shell-only，相对提升 64% [S5.p1]。在 HumanEvalFix 上，SWE-agent 取得 88.3% 的 pass@1 率 [S5.p2]。消融显示，没有搜索工具时性能为 15.7%，迭代搜索反而降至 12.0%；没有文件编辑器时降至 10.3%；没有 linting 时降至 15.0% [S5.SS1.p3][S5.SS1.p4][S5.SS1.p5]。行为分析发现，智能体通常先复现和/或定位问题，之后主要是“编辑再执行”循环 [S5.SS2.p2][S5.SS2.p3]；2,294 个任务实例中有 1,185 个（51.7%）的轨迹出现至少一次失败编辑 [S5.SS2.p4]；成功运行比不成功运行完成更早、成本更低 [S5.SS2.p5]；约一半（52.0%）未解决实例属于错误实现或过度特定实现 [S5.SS2.p6]。

evidence.quote: SWE-agent w/ GPT-4 Turbo achieves the best performance all-around, successfully solving $12.47$ % ( $286$ / $2,294$) of the full SWE-bench test set and $18.00$ % ( $54$ / $300$) of the Lite split.
compared to RAG on Lite, SWE-agent is $8$ - $13$ x more costly but yields a $6.7$ -fold improved % Resolved rate.
An LM-friendly ACI’s value is confirmed by SWE-agent’s $64$ % relative increase compared to Shell-only, both with GPT-4 Turbo.
SWE-agent yields strong performance on HumanEvalFix with $88.3$ % pass@1 rate.
leading to even worse performance than the not having additional search tools at all ( $15.7$ % $\downarrow$ 2.3 for No search vs. $12.0$ % $\downarrow$ 6.0 with Iterative search).
Without SWE-agent’s file editor interface, performance drops to ( $10.3$ % $\downarrow$ 7.7).
This intervention improves performance considerably (without linting, $15.0$ % $\downarrow$ 3.0).
SWE-agent usually begins with either writing reproduction code and/or localizing the issue’s cause to specific lines of code.
from turn $5$ onwards, the most frequent two actions for all turns are edit and python.
out of $2,294$ task instances, $1,185$ ( $51.7$ %) of SWE-agent w/ GPT-4 Turbo trajectories have $1$ + failed edits.
We observe that successful runs complete earlier and at a cheaper cost than unsuccessful ones.
about half ( $52.0$ %) of unresolved instances fall into the Incorrect Implementation or Overly Specific Implementation categories
